Dave Roberts’ decisions questioned after Dodgers lose Game 3 to Brewers
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts' strategic decisions during Game 3 against Milwaukee are under scrutiny following key pinch-hitting moves and pitching choices. The team's offensive struggles contributed further as they lost both Game 3 and were swept from the series.
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts made several costly mistakes in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers, mistakes that ultimately played into the loss, according to an Oct. 14 report.
Roberts made several questionable choices in the sixth and seventh innings, and the Brewers capitalized on them. In the sixth inning, Teoscar Hernandez allowed a leadoff walk, while Kyle Tucker walked shortly after. With Andy Pages, one of the best hitters this postseason and an elite defender, due up, Roberts pulled Pages for Max Muncy to face right-handed pitcher Abner Uribe. Muncy struck out swinging, but Shohei Ohtani drew a walk to load the bases with one out. Will Smith then hit a double that scored two runs and gave Los Angeles a 2-1 lead.
The decision-making continued when Roberts had Josue De Paula pinch-hit for Miguel Rojas before Milwaukee made its bullpen call. When left-hander DL Hall emerged from the bullpen instead of Uribe staying in, Roberts replaced De Paula with Kike Hernandez as a pinch-hitter. This move left only Hunter Feduccia available as a potential pinch-hitter later in the game. Kike Hernandez struck out swinging and no one could pinch-hit for Tommy Edman, who also struck out.
De Paula is considered by many to be "the team’s most talented and surging hitter," so losing him without an at-bat was described as brutal given that Los Angeles did not score again after the sixth inning.
In pitching decisions during the top of the seventh inning, Blake Snell walked his first batter after six innings but remained in despite struggling with command. Snell then allowed a home run to Jake Bauers on his eleventh pitch of that at-bat and stayed in for another at-bat where he gave up another home run on a changeup pitch—giving Milwaukee a 4-2 lead.
Ultimately, it was noted that "the Dodgers’ hitters failed to deliver for most of the game and throughout the series," contributing significantly to their position along with underperformance from their starting rotation.
